artifact: cycle 3: hidden-mode pulse-order separation under pointwise chemical-Langevin equality
scope: Exact finite-state mathematical construction, internal numerical checks, and a bounded primary-literature comparison; no biological data were analyzed.

claims.claim: For the stated four-species fixed-stoichiometry burst CTMC, the two mechanisms have equal full-state chemical-Langevin drift and covariance at every state and allowed action, and also equal third jump-moment tensors; their fourth distinct-coordinate jump moments differ.
claims.evidence: Every coordinate subset of size at most three has inclusion probability 2^(-|I|) under both mask laws; the fourfold inclusion is 1/16 versus 1/8. Derivation is in CYCLE3_REPORT.md.
claims.limitations: This is a constructed jump model with simultaneous multi-species burst channels; it is not evidence for a particular biochemical mechanism.

claims.claim: Under a stationary uniform hidden-phase prior and parity-only observation, passive and one-letter data are equal across mechanisms; AA and BB are also equal; a mixed two-letter word is the minimum possible separating word in the specified model.
claims.evidence: Hidden-phase rotation conjugacy for one-letter B and BB; identical A kernels for A and AA; exact AB matrix-exponential law and positive κ=0 increment association.
claims.limitations: Requires the specified known phase-shift structure and uniform prior; not a universal minimum-word theorem for hidden Markov models.

claims.claim: For AB pulses of duration 0.38, r=1, endpoint error epsilon=0.08, and unknown clockwise hidden switching rate κ in [0,3], a binary event has disjoint mechanism probability ranges with a certified gap at least 0.0049987462; 239779 independent wells suffice for 5% error by Hoeffding.
claims.evidence: 30001-point scan, per-model Duhamel Lipschitz bound 1.52, threshold 0.0747219986, and finite-sample Hoeffding bound in CYCLE3_REPORT.md and CYCLE3_MODEL_OUTPUT.json.
claims.limitations: r and epsilon are treated as calibrated known values, κ must lie in the declared compact interval, and independent wells are required. The sample size is sufficient and conservative, not necessary.

claims.claim: As hidden switching becomes arbitrarily fast, both mechanisms have the same action-averaged burst law, so any fixed finite snapshot experiment loses uniform separation; an unbounded-rate controller must permit UNKNOWN.
claims.evidence: Each action is in its iid phase one-third of the time in both models; noisy endpoint TV numerically tends to zero for κ=3,6,10,30,100.
claims.limitations: The reported finite TV values are checks; the limiting statement is for the stated finite-state hidden-phase generator and bounded finite pulse programs.

claims.claim: A batch-adaptive finite-action acquisition rule using exact four-category predictions, conditional Hoeffding radii, a summable error schedule, and cost-normalized worst-case separation can stop when one mechanism confidence set empties and otherwise return UNKNOWN at its cap.
claims.evidence: Sequential design and confidence-set rule in CYCLE3_REPORT.md.
claims.limitations: It adapts the word across replicate-well batches, not within a well after a noisy first-pulse observation; uncertain r, reporter error, or actuation parameters require inclusion in the nuisance set and a recomputed separation certificate.

claims.claim: The scaling-and-squaring CTMC exponentials and matrix-exponential endpoint probabilities agree with an independent Poisson-uniformization implementation to at most 6.66e-16 for the checked parameters.
claims.limitations: Numerical implementation verification only; no proof assistant or external computational validation was used.

claims.claim: A real cell-fate system satisfies the hidden-cycle, burst stoichiometry, parity reporter, pulse-rate, noise, or switching-rate assumptions and will follow the predicted AB response.
claims.evidence: No biological data, lineages, drugs, cell lines, or empirical pulse parameters were supplied or analyzed.
claims.limitations: Requires reporter calibration, independently randomized lineage-resolved wells, rate bounds, and held-out pulse-order experiments.

claims.claim: The exact CLE-matched construction or pulse-word certificate is novel relative to all prior work.
claims.limitations: Generic biochemical model discrimination and input/pulse design are established; no exhaustive novelty search was done.
